title: The G.G. Shinobi II: The Silent Fury
subtitle: The crystals and their guardians
summary: The G.G. Shinobi II: The Silent Fury is Sega's ninja platform sequel, released for Game Gear in 1992, with the Japanese edition arriving on 11 December.
body: The G.G. Shinobi II: The Silent Fury is Sega's ninja platform sequel, released for Game Gear in 1992, with the Japanese edition arriving on 11 December. Joe Musashi and his allies seek five elemental crystals taken by the Techno-Warriors and their Black Ninja. The coloured ninja team returns, with each character supplying a particular combination of weapon, movement and magic. Stages can again be approached in different orders, making the campaign's structure depend on which companion has already been rescued and what that companion allows the player to reach.

The opening four stages each contain a captured ally and an elemental crystal, but rescuing the ninja does not always make the crystal immediately accessible. A particular ability may be required, sending the player elsewhere before returning with the appropriate companion. The route through the campaign therefore develops across several visits rather than simply ending each stage once. New weapons and revised abilities change the earlier game's combinations, while hidden health upgrades reward looking beyond the direct path. A return journey can reveal an opportunity that the initial rescue left unresolved.

Gathering the first four crystals opens the enemy's main base and the final confrontation over the fifth. By that point, the available team supplies the abilities required to face the remaining obstacles. A password system supports returning to the portable adventure later, fitting the connected campaign into shorter sessions. Yuzo Koshiro and Motohiro Kawashima composed the music. The sequel strengthens the relationship between rescuing characters and exploring stages: another ninja changes the possibilities in several places, so the team grows into a practical map of routes the player can now complete.
